title: THE NEXT STOP — A railway mix-up told through two travelers and two matching cases, 24 deliverables

config.text:
# THE NEXT STOP

## Project
- Runtime: 36 seconds.
- Shot count: 6.
- Shot duration: 6 seconds each.
- Act 1: 0–12 seconds; boarding and correct ownership.
- Act 2: 12–24 seconds; mistaken pickup and recognition.
- Act 3: 24–36 seconds; meeting and return.
- Audience: families with children aged 6–10; character-channel followers.
- Viewing context: family viewing on a character channel.
- Tone: gentle comedy, a brief moment of concern, shared relief.
- Printed title: THE NEXT STOP.
- Dialogue line 1: This one is yours.
- Dialogue line 2: Back where it belongs.

## Character identities
| Attribute | Pip | Rowan |
|---|---|---|
| Species | Upright otter | Upright otter |
| Height, including ears | 1000 mm | 1200 mm |
| Head-to-total-height ratio | 1:4 | 1:4 |
| Fur | Cinnamon #9A6244 | Dark brown #5B463B |
| Muzzle | Cream #EAD9B8 | Cream #EAD9B8 |
| Clothing | Mustard coat #C99A32 | Moss-green vest #5D7356 |
| Identity detail | Navy square patch #263B50 on left elbow | Round navy glasses #263B50 |
| Feet | Bare rounded paws | Bare rounded paws |
| Tail | Short tapered otter tail | Short tapered otter tail |
| Expressions | Neutral; surprised; relieved | Neutral; surprised; relieved |
| Owned case | Star tag | Circle tag |
| Shared-view screen position | Left | Right |

## Case construction
- Quantity: 2.
- Overall dimensions including fixed handle and wheels: 550 mm high × 360 mm wide × 220 mm deep.
- Shell: hard shell, #356B70, rounded corners.
- Front: 3 vertical raised ribs.
- Wheels: 2 black wheels on the lower rear edge.
- Handle: 1 fixed black top handle.
- Closure: black zipper around the side seam.
- Handle tag: navy #263B50, 60 × 45 mm, attached to the top handle.
- Pip's tag symbol: centered ivory #F4E8CC five-point star.
- Rowan's tag symbol: centered ivory #F4E8CC circle.
- Difference between the two cases: tag symbol only.

## Carriage geometry
- Interior length: 6000 mm.
- Interior width: 2800 mm.
- Coordinate origin: rear-left interior corner.
- Longitudinal x-axis: rear to front, 0–6000 mm.
- Transverse y-axis: vehicle left to vehicle right, 0–2800 mm.
- Central aisle: y = 1100–1700 mm; width 600 mm.
- Seat banks: x = 1400–2000 mm and 3000–3600 mm; paired seats on each side of the aisle.
- Forward-left luggage rack: x = 4800–5400 mm, y = 0–1100 mm; shelf height 450 mm.
- Yellow grab pole: x = 4500 mm, y = 1000 mm.
- Side-door openings: x = 5400–6000 mm, on both vehicle sides; opening height 1900 mm.
- Interior camera area: aisle, x = 600–4500 mm.
- Exterior camera area: right-side platform beside the door end.
- Platform side convention: left or right while facing the train's direction of travel.

## Color and composition
- Act 1 light: warm #F3D9A4.
- Act 2 light: cool #B9CDD8.
- Act 3 light: warm #F3D9A4.
- Landscape composition: 16:9.
- Portrait composition: 9:16.
- Action-safe inset: 3.5% from each edge in both compositions.
- Graphics-safe inset: 5% from each edge in both compositions.
- Shot-size vocabulary: WS = wide shot; MS = medium shot; CU = close-up.
- Storyboard panel metadata: shot ID; shot size; parent-shot duration; character names.
- Phase-frame metadata: offset in seconds within the parent shot.
- Case-symbol treatment: visible tag or detail inset for oblique views.

## Dialogue and animatic timing
- Subtitle position: bottom-centered inside the graphics-safe area.
- Subtitle capacity: at most 2 lines per cue.
- Subtitle duration range: 5/6 second to 7 seconds.
- Pip's subtitle cue: 22–24 seconds; duration 2 seconds.
- Rowan's subtitle cue: 32–35 seconds; duration 3 seconds.
- Reserved audio-description interval: 24–30 seconds, between the two dialogue cues.
- Title appearance: 35–36 seconds, upper-center inside the graphics-safe area.
- Animatic excerpt: S05–S06; story time 24–36 seconds; playback time 0–12 seconds.
- Animatic dialogue cue: playback 8–11 seconds.
- Animatic title cue: playback 11–12 seconds.

# THE NEXT STOP: story records

## Three-act synopsis
| Act | Interval | Synopsis |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0–12 seconds | Pip and Rowan board at Willow Quay with their own cases. Pip places the star case beside Rowan's circle case on the forward-left rack. They settle into nearby seats as the train departs. |
| 2 | 12–24 seconds | At Juniper Halt, the opening doors prompt both travelers to collect their luggage for the next stop. Each takes the nearest case, swapping ownership, and both remain aboard. As the train leaves, they notice the unfamiliar symbols and recognize the mistake. |
| 3 | 24–36 seconds | They step onto the right-side platform at Orchard End and turn toward each other. A shared glance leads to the exchange. Both leave with their own case and a relieved smile. |

## Station sequence
| Order | Station | Platform side facing travel | Story placement | Traveler movement |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| 2 | Juniper Halt | Left | S03; departure in S04 | Both remain aboard with swapped cases |
| 3 | Orchard End | Right | S05–S06 | Both alight and exchange cases |

steps.userMessage:
THE NEXT STOP | A railway mix-up told through two travelers and two matching cases

We are developing a 36-second animated railway adventure for family viewing on our character channel. The story follows Pip and Rowan from Willow Quay through Juniper Halt to Orchard End: they board with their own cases, accidentally take each other's case at the intermediate stop, discover the mistake and exchange them at their destination. Use the attached six-shot story, with each shot lasting 6 seconds and each act occupying 12 seconds. The tone is gently comic, with the recognition carried by hands, glances and luggage details. Print "THE NEXT STOP" on the character sheet, shot table and final storyboard panel. The two spoken lines are "This one is yours." and "Back where it belongs."

The existing characters and cases set the direction. Pip is a 1000 mm tall cinnamon otter with a cream muzzle, a mustard coat and a navy square patch on the left elbow. Rowan is a 1200 mm tall dark-brown otter with a cream muzzle, round glasses and a moss-green vest. Both cases have a #356B70 shell, three vertical ribs, two black wheels and a black top handle; each measures 550 × 360 × 220 mm, height × width × depth. Their sole distinguishing feature is an ivory symbol on a navy handle tag: Pip owns the star case and Rowan owns the circle case. The carriage has a 600 mm central aisle, a forward-left luggage rack and a yellow pole beside that rack. Platform sides follow the station table. Use warm #F3D9A4 light for Acts 1 and 3 and cooler #B9CDD8 light for Act 2. Compose the story in both 16:9 and 9:16, with action inset 3.5% and graphics inset 5% from every edge. Recompose each shot for the vertical version, with the subjects inside both versions' action-safe areas.

Audience: families with children aged 6–10 and followers of our character channel, with the work supporting our producer's story approval and the animation team's shot planning.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md records the character anchors, luggage construction, palette and screen rules. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists the deliverables and their proportions, formats and stages. 03-story-records.en.md contains the three-act synopsis, station sequence, six timed shots and dialogue cues. landscape-safe-area.png supplies the 16:9 action and graphics boundaries. portrait-safe-area.png supplies the corresponding 9:16 boundaries. carriage-and-stations.png supplies the carriage geometry, camera areas and platform sides. travelers-identity.png supplies the existing appearances of Pip and Rowan. matching-cases-identity.png supplies the case construction and the two ownership symbols. carriage-daylight-reference.png supplies the daylight, upholstery and window-reflection atmosphere.

Deliverables:
1. One two-page character, color and timing specification recording the fixed anchors, palette, six-shot structure, act intervals, dialogue cues and the 24–30 second pause reserved for audio description
2. One finished character sheet showing Pip and Rowan in front, side and back views, each with neutral, surprised and relieved expressions, their heights and clothing colors
3. One six-row shot table covering S01–S06, with shot size, duration, characters, action, dialogue, subtitle cues and case ownership
4. One six-frame color script covering S01–S06 in order, with the act colors and the 36-second timeline
5. Nine finished keyframes: S01 ownership at the rack, S02 seated travel, S03 the mistaken pickup and its hand detail, S04 recognition and its tag detail, S05 the platform meeting, and S06 the exchange and closing smiles
6. Nine storyboard sheets: one complete six-shot sheet; three act sheets with two successive action phases per shot; and five performance sheets for S01, S02, S03, S04 and S05, each with three successive phases within that shot; every frame paired with a recomposed 9:16 version of its 16:9 composition
7. One 12-second landscape animatic of S05–S06, using the storyboard actions, the character sheet, the final dialogue cue and the title appearance
8. One production presentation of at least twelve pages, reusing the specification, character sheet, shot table, color script, nine keyframes, nine storyboard sheets and frames from the animatic

Acceptance:
- The specification comes first and records six shots, 36 seconds, Pip at 1000 mm, Rowan at 1200 mm and the two act-lighting colors. The character sheet repeats both heights and the clothing anchors; the shot table and presentation repeat the shot count, total duration and act intervals; the color script and presentation repeat both lighting codes.
- The character sheet contains six views and six expressions. All nine keyframes, nine storyboard sheets, the color script and animatic preserve its cream muzzles, Pip's mustard coat and left-elbow navy patch, Rowan's round glasses and moss-green vest, and the cases' three ribs, two wheels and ownership symbols.
- The shot table, storyboard and animatic preserve the six-shot station and ownership sequence: star with Pip and circle with Rowan in S01–S02, circle with Pip and star with Rowan in S03–S05, and the return during S06. Every storyboard frame prints shot ID, WS, MS or CU, the parent shot's 6-second duration and character names; act and performance phases also print their offsets within that shot. Shared views keep Pip screen-left and Rowan screen-right, with case symbols legible through detail insets when needed.
- The complete storyboard contains six landscape–portrait pairs, each act sheet contains four pairs and each performance sheet contains three pairs. Both versions use 3.5% action and 5% graphics margins. The nine keyframes and storyboard retain the forward-left rack, yellow pole and recorded platform sides wherever visible, while their lighting follows the color script's #F3D9A4 for S01–S02 and S05–S06 and #B9CDD8 for S03–S04.
- The storyboard and shot table reproduce both dialogue lines with bottom-centered subtitle boxes of at most two lines and cues lasting 2 and 3 seconds. The animatic maps story time 24–36 seconds to playback time 0–12 seconds, preserves the 24–30 second dialogue pause, captions Back where it belongs. at playback 8–11 seconds and carries THE NEXT STOP at 11–12 seconds.
- The presentation has at least twelve pages, states THE NEXT STOP, six shots and 36 seconds on its first page, and reuses all seven earlier deliverable categories. Its shot-by-shot account places all nine keyframes and all nine storyboard sheets against the six-shot timeline and locates the character anchors, pickup, recognition and return.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
